clue.text: You can't immediately see what's written in this

definitions.text: You can't immediately see what's written in this

parts.words: You can't immediately see what's written in this
parts.note: a writing fluid whose marks stay unseen until heat or a chemical brings them out, so a message in it cannot be read at once

explanation.surface: A remark about a page whose text is hard to make out at first glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret writing fluids leave marks that only show up later when treated, so the words are not readable straight away.

clue.text: A car should be kept under cover

definitions.text: A car should be kept under cover

parts.words: A car should be kept under cover
parts.note: the surface suggests a garage or tarpaulin, but the cover meant is a policy against accident or theft, which the law requires for a car

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a motor in a garage out of the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under cover' looks like shelter from rain; read it as insurance cover, which every car on the road should have.
explanation.definitionFit: Being protected by an insurance policy is being 'covered', so a car with a policy is kept under cover.

clue.text: Value gt model in an old book?

indicators.note: to model is to shape or form, so these letters are moulded into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A garbled note asking whether some valued model appears in an antique volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'model' signals rearranging the seven letters VALUEGT; 'gt' is just two letters of fodder and makes no word on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth-century Latin translation of the Bible by St Jerome is an ancient book, the standard Catholic text for centuries.

clue.text: Cynic heard about my refusal to come up with the same definition

indicators.note: about means the sound-alike goes around the next part
heard tells us to use the sound of the word cynic rather than its spelling

parts.note: a cynic, said aloud, gives the sound written here with S and Y

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the words my and refusal are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a refusal is a no

explanation.surface: A sceptic is overheard rejecting a request to produce a matching meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' asks for the sound of Cynic, spelt with S and Y; 'to come up' turns 'my refusal' upwards into ONYM, and 'about' wraps the sound-alike round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A word that is a synonym of another shares its meaning, so synonymic words have the same sense.

clue.text: It may provide high jinks in noisy barracks

indicators.note: noisy tells us the answer is a word that sounds like the next one

parts.note: to barrack is to jeer, so barracks here means boos

explanation.surface: Soldiers living in a loud army barracks get up to rowdy fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barracks' looks like soldiers' quarters, but it is the verb: a crowd barracks a player by booing. Barracking is a British and Australian term for jeering.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong drink tends to lead to rowdy fun and pranks, so alcohol may be the source of high jinks.

clue.text: Select additional court

parts.note: additional means extra

explanation.surface: A choice between an extra court, perhaps at a tennis club.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to pick out or take a chosen part from a larger whole, as when choosing a passage.

clue.text: Writer looking up melody, part of Holst suite

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the word for the writer is read upwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
a melody is a tune

explanation.surface: A composer glances up from a tune that forms one movement of an orchestral work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking up' turns the writer upside down in this down clue, giving NEP. Holst's suite is The Planets, one movement per planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst's orchestral suite The Planets has a movement for each planet, the last subtitled 'the Mystic'.

clue.text: Sweet flattery needs 4, perhaps

parts.note: to butter someone up is to flatter them, so flattery is butter
the answer to 4 down is drink, and whisky from Scotland is one example of it

explanation.surface: Sweet talk needs a strong drink to go with it.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' refers to the answer of clue 4 down (drink); 'perhaps' marks Scotch whisky as one example of that.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard toffee made from brown sugar and butter is a type of confectionery, a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Greek character you found eavesdropping!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Greek character you found eavesdropping!' (7): 'you' gives U, but no parse of 'found eavesdropping' gives the remaining PSILON, and no blog or database gives one

clue.text: Work by the month for this influential organisation

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the month goes next to the work

parts.note: OCT is the abbreviation for October, a month
an opus is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a job paid monthly for a powerful body.
explanation.walkthrough: An organisation with many far-reaching arms of influence is figuratively called an eight-limbed sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An organisation with branches reaching everywhere is likened to the many-armed sea creature, a common figurative sense.

clue.text: Pink dessert placed before bill

parts.note: in British usage a dessert course is a sweet
Bill is a short form of the name William

explanation.surface: A pudding is placed on the table before the bill arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink' looks like a colour, but it is a flower: sweet william belongs to the pink family, Dianthus.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet william is Dianthus barbatus, a garden flower of the same genus as the pinks and carnations.

clue.text: Land creature not keeping quiet

indicators.note: not keeping means the letter for quiet is dropped from the creature

parts.note: a terrapin is a creature, a freshwater turtle
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: An animal on dry ground refuses to stay silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is ground or a stretch of country, as in rough or hilly land.

clue.text: The result of the rubber?

parts.note: the surface suggests the outcome of a series of games at bridge, but the rubber is an eraser, and its result is something rubbed out

explanation.surface: A question about who won the deciding set of games at bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: A rubber is a series of games in bridge or cricket; in British English it is also a pencil eraser.
explanation.definitionFit: Using an eraser removes marks, so a rubbing-out is what a rubber produces.

clue.text: It's clear, say, around the brow of the hill

parts.note: to clear is to rid

indicators.note: around means the abbreviation for say is turned round

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the top of a hill is plainly visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal, but here it turns the abbreviation round, giving GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The long narrow top of a hill is its crest, the line along its summit.

clue.text: Strongest eight loses cohesion in fog

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters go inside the word for fog

parts.note: fog is mist

indicators.note: something that loses cohesion falls apart, so the letters of eight are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A rowing crew of eight falls apart in thick fog despite being the strongest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses cohesion' breaks up the number into IGHTE, and 'in' sets that inside the word for fog.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty means very powerful, so its superlative describes the most powerful.

clue.text: Bitterness over an attempt to show bravery

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the bitterness sits above the rest

parts.note: gall is bitterness or rancour
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Resentment of a failed effort turns into a display of courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage in battle or danger is called gallantry, as in medals for valour.

clue.text: Categorise one with state kind of education

parts.note: to categorise is to class
I is the Roman numeral for one
CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Sorting someone together with a state school's type of teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooling grounded in Latin and Greek language and literature is the traditional humanities education.

clue.text: What's bland could get one annoyed

indicators.note: the letters of annoyed could get, by rearrangement, a new word; the phrase also echoes 'get one annoyed'

explanation.surface: Something dull and inoffensive can still irritate people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could get one' signals rearranging ANNOYED; the surface reading, that blandness irritates, is a neat paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodyne means inoffensive and unlikely to provoke, so something insipid and dull.

clue.text: Father restrains a commissioned officer getting cross

indicators.note: restrains means the word for father holds the next letters inside it

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a father
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, a commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A father holds back an army officer who is becoming angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry; it is the diagonal cross of heraldry, as in the Scottish flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal cross shaped like an X, as on the flag of Scotland.

clue.text: Lodged in public house — railway inn?

indicators.note: lodged in means the answer is lodged inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A guest stays in a pub that might be a railway hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'house — railway'. A serai is a caravanserai, an inn for travellers in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A serai is a caravanserai, a resting place for travellers and their caravans in Asia.

clue.text: Organisation of a masque tips the scales

indicators.note: the organisation of letters is their arrangement, so the letters of a masque are put in a new order

explanation.surface: The way a court masque is staged tips the balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organisation of' rearranges A MASQUE; 'tips' is a link here, though it pretends to belong to 'tips the scales'.
explanation.definitionFit: Squamae is the Latin plural used in biology for the scales on fish, reptiles and some plants.

clue.text: Deserter keeps solution of code for old soldier

indicators.note: keeps means the deserter holds the rearranged letters inside

parts.note: a rat is someone who deserts a cause

indicators.note: the solution of a code reworks it, so the letters of code are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deserter holds the key to a cipher used by a veteran soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solution of' scrambles the cipher word into EDCO, and 'keeps' sets it inside the deserter; a rat is one who abandons a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoats were British soldiers of past centuries, named for their scarlet tunics.

clue.text: Casually went and played the flute

definitions.meaning: to tootle is to travel along in a leisurely way
to tootle is also to toot gently on a wind instrument

explanation.definitionFit: Tootle means both to drive or stroll along unhurriedly and to blow a pipe or horn softly.

clue.text: Live and be successful without love?

indicators.note: without means the letter for love is taken away

parts.note: to do well is to be successful
love is zero in tennis scoring, written O

explanation.surface: A question of whether one can live happily and thrive with no love.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside or make a home somewhere.

clue.text: A race conducted round Sussex town

parts.note: a race is a run

indicators.note: round means the word for conducted is turned the other way

parts.note: conducted means led

explanation.surface: A race is staged around a town in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns 'conducted' backwards, giving DEL. Arundel is a castle town in West Sussex, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Arundel is a historic town in West Sussex, known for its castle and cathedral.

clue.text: Why a furious rage becomes erratic?

indicators.note: furious means wild and agitated, so the letters of why a are thrown into disorder

parts.note: rage is ire

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why someone's anger turns unpredictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' scrambles the first two words into HAYW; 'furious rage' reads as one phrase but splits between indicator and synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To go haywire is to malfunction or behave wildly out of control, a colloquial idiom.

clue.text: A fair kind of lottery?

parts.note: the surface suggests an honest draw, but the fair meant is a fete or carnival, where prize draws from a drum are a staple

explanation.surface: A question about whether a lottery is run honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like honest, but it is the noun: a fete or fairground. A tombola is a British fete raffle with tickets drawn from a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: At British fetes and fairs, a prize draw with tickets pulled from a revolving drum is a popular raffle.

clue.text: Capturing gambit pieces, craftily deter new movement of forces

indicators.note: capturing means the rearranged letters hold the next pieces inside them
craftily means cunningly worked, so the letters of deter are rearranged

parts.note: a gambit is a ploy
in chess the pieces are called men

explanation.surface: A chess player taking pieces with a gambit cunningly deters an army's fresh manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craftily' scrambles 'deter' into REDET; 'Capturing' sets the gambit and the chess pieces inside it, just before its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Redeploying troops shifts them to a different place or task, a fresh positioning of the armed forces.
